judgment.rationale: The report provides a detailed and repeatable elevated-terminal sequence, a non-elevated control, version and OS details, and a current triage comment confirming that reproduction is sufficient. It does not yet establish the failing symbol or safe implementation change.
evidence: The issue is open, labeled Issue-Bug and Product-Command Palette, and updated by the triage comment on 2026-09-27.
The reporter describes an unelevated Command Palette launching an elevated terminal through Ctrl+Enter, after which only Microsoft.CmdPal.UI exits silently.
The report includes a control test showing that an elevated process launched outside Command Palette does not terminate it.
The report states there are no crash, WER, exception, or error-log records and that non-elevated launches continue to work.
The automated triage comment marks reproduction as sufficient and does not request another diagnostic archive.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the elevated-child launch on a current build, then trace the parent lifetime and elevation helper before designing a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is reproducible, but the failing launcher or WinGet initialization boundary has not been confirmed from repository evidence; no speculative design is emitted in this lightweight pass.

issue_context.summary: An unelevated Command Palette exits silently after launching an elevated terminal through its own admin action, while the elevated child succeeds and externally launched elevated processes do not affect the palette.
known_information: The report targets Command Palette 0.12.12365.0 shipped with PowerToys 0.101.2362.0.
The repro uses an unelevated PowerToys/Command Palette instance and Ctrl+Enter or an elevated terminal profile.
The elevated terminal opens, but Microsoft.CmdPal.UI disappears and must be relaunched.
The reporter supplied a control test, event-log/WER observations, locale, Windows build, UAC settings, and WinGet configuration.
The latest triage comment marks reproduction sufficient.
inferences: The failure likely lies in the Command Palette elevation or child-process lifetime path rather than the mere presence of an elevated process, but the exact failing branch is unconfirmed.
issue_context.analysis: The public evidence is sufficient for maintainer-side reproduction and narrows the investigation to the in-process elevated-launch path. A design should wait until a current build confirms whether the parent exits through launcher error handling, package activation, or WinGet initialization.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body, the single triage comment, labels, and live update timestamp.
Confirmed the issue already contains a control test and does not need a repeated request for generic diagnostics.
Checked the local CmdPal source tree for elevation-related paths; no exact root cause was established during the lightweight pass.

reproduce.title: Replay issue #50822
prerequisites: Run PowerToys and Command Palette unelevated.
Have an elevated terminal profile or use the Ctrl+Enter run-as-administrator action.
steps: Open Command Palette and search for a terminal.
Launch the terminal with the elevated/admin action.
Confirm that the elevated terminal opens.
Check whether Microsoft.CmdPal.UI remains running and whether the Command Palette hotkey can reopen it.
Repeat with a non-elevated terminal launch and with an elevated process started outside Command Palette as controls.
reproduce.expected_result: The elevated child opens and Command Palette remains running and reusable.
